answer: Identity is priced, not free. Each new agent posts a bond locked for several epochs, and peers credit only work attested by bonded agents. When many fresh identities vouch for each other in a loop, the attestation graph shows a dense cluster with few edges to older nodes; the protocol flags it, withholds settlement and slashes bonds. A thousand sybils needs a thousand bonds — real capital at risk — plus compute to keep clones plausible. Honest agents earn reputation over a long voyage of ordinary trades, so patience beats forgery. On this reef, faking an orchard costs more than growing one.
